solvers.cpsat: CP-SAT exact model, 1 search worker, random_seed=42, stops at the time limit
solvers.clarke_wright: Clarke-Wright savings, one deterministic pass; ignores the time limit
solvers.ortools: OR-Tools routing, PATH_CHEAPEST_ARC + GUIDED_LOCAL_SEARCH until the time limit; the search has no random seed, so results vary only with how much search fits in the time limit

provenance.runtime_note: runtime_seconds is wall time of the whole solver call, model building included
provenance.distance_note: Solvers work on integers: distance = Euclidean x 100 rounded, travel time = Euclidean x 100 rounded up (so every validated schedule is feasible in real arithmetic). Reported distance is recomputed from the coordinates in double precision; distance_one_decimal truncates each arc to one decimal.
provenance.gap_note: 100 customers: gap_percent = (distance - reference) / reference vs the SINTEF best known. 25/50 customers: gap_percent = (distance_one_decimal - reference) / reference vs Solomon's proven optima. gap_measured_on names the field compared. null when there is no feasible solution or no published reference.
provenance.optimality_note: proven_optimal_scaled_model is CP-SAT's optimality proof on the integer model above, not on the reference's convention. Travel time rounded up makes that model stricter, so a proven solution can still have a positive gap_percent.

data.instances: Solomon (1987) VRPTW instances, SINTEF TOP backup
data.subsets: 25/50-customer versions are the first 25/50 customers of each 100-customer file

sintef_best_known.title: SINTEF TOP, Solomon benchmark, 100 customers: best known solutions
sintef_best_known.objective: hierarchical: 1) minimize number of vehicles, 2) minimize total distance
sintef_best_known.distance_convention: Euclidean distance and time in double precision; total distance rounded to two decimals
sintef_best_known.notes: r111 is quoted by SINTEF as 1096.73* (checker value 1096.72658305008); r205 and rc101 carry SINTEF's footnote that earlier values 994.42 / 1696.94 came from a rounding error.

solomon_optimal.title: M. M. Solomon, Optimal Solutions for C1/C2, R1/R2 and RC1/RC2 problems (last updated 2005-03-24)
solomon_optimal.objective: minimize total distance (vehicle count is whatever the optimal routes use)
solomon_optimal.distance_convention: exact-method convention: each arc's Euclidean distance (and travel time) truncated to one decimal. Checked here: CP-SAT with truncated one-decimal arithmetic reproduces the published optima (e.g. C101.25 = 191.3, R101.25 = 617.1, RC101.25 = 461.1).
